name: Han Dongli
current_role: Founder/chairman (per Hurun 2010), Dongli Industrial Group (China) - current status unverified
profile: Listed on the Hurun China 2010 rich list with ~US$150M from Dongli Industrial Group, active in hematite (iron ore), cement and industrial filter cloth. No current public profile, company website or press coverage could be found online in English or Chinese.
notes: Very low public footprint; only appearance found is Hurun 2010. Searches for 韩东立 / 东立实业集团 returned nothing relevant. Would need a Chinese business registry (e.g. National Enterprise Credit system) to locate the company; not a practical podcast target without a local intermediary.

name: B Umapathy Reddy
current_role: Founder director / head (listed as Managing Director in registry data), BGR Mining & Infra Ltd, Hyderabad
profile: Bathina Umapathy Reddy co-founded BGR (originally B Girijapathi Reddy & Co.) in 1988 with Girijapathy Reddy and I. Sudhakara Reddy. It is now a Hyderabad-based contract-mining and Mine Developer & Operator (MDO) group running coal and mineral projects for NTPC, CCL, Vedanta and Hindalco. He still leads the group alongside the second generation.
interesting_fact: BGR says it runs 900+ dump trucks and 8,000+ employees across 7 states. It has won a string of coal MDO contracts, including NTPC's Kerendari 'A' (2023) and Badam (2024) and Hindalco's Meenakshi (2025).
deep_cut_fact: BGR began in 1988 as a small partnership firm, B Girijapathi Reddy & Co., set up by three co-founders including Umapathy Reddy. It became a company only in 2011, and by FY2022-23 it was moving about 29 million tonnes of coal a year.
notes: Low personal media profile. The company publishes only a careers email (careers@bgrmining.com) and a Hyderabad office line, so the contact form or the corporate office is the best route. Relevant to the energy angle as a coal mining contractor.

name: Kulanthaivel Vinayagam
current_role: Managing Director, SCM Group / The Chennai Silks; Group MD, Space Textiles Pvt Ltd
profile: K. Vinayagam (also spelled Vinayakam) is one of the brothers who run SCM Group, the family textile empire founded by A. Kulandaivel Mudaliar, best known for the South Indian retail chain The Chennai Silks. The group also spins yarn, exports hosiery and garments to brands such as Decathlon and Hanes, and runs precast-construction, school and hospital ventures.
interesting_fact: In 2007 The Chennai Silks set a Guinness record for the world's most expensive silk saree, worth about Rs 41 lakh. It reproduced 11 Raja Ravi Varma paintings and took around 4,760 hours to design.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as a Khadi shop, Kasthuribhai Khadi Vasthralayam in Madurai (1962). Today it is run jointly by eight brothers, four sisters and their children, about 130 family members, and spins roughly 130 tonnes of yarn a day on 170,000 spindles.
notes: Low individual media profile; family-run group led publicly by chairman T.K. Chandiran. His son V. Vikram Narayen is Executive Director. The best route is the corporate office via the official website. Spelling varies (Vinayagam/Vinayakam).

name: Li Jianhong
current_role: Unverified - associated (per Hurun 2005-2008) with Yinjiang Jinghong Investment
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China rich lists 2005-2008 with ~US$130M, attributed to Yinjiang Jinghong Investment in communications and property. No current online profile, company website or press coverage could be found to confirm his present role.
notes: Common name; nothing found linking 李建宏 to a Yinjiang/Jinghong entity. Unrelated to the listed smart-city firm Enjoyor (银江股份), whose leadership is different. He has been off the lists since 2008. A Chinese business-registry lookup would be needed; not a practical podcast target.

name: Theresa E Wagler
current_role: EVP & CFO, Steel Dynamics (becomes President & CEO on 1 Jan 2027); Director, CF Industries
profile: Theresa Wagler is a former Ernst & Young CPA who joined steelmaker Steel Dynamics in 1998, when it was still a fast-growing startup. She became CFO in 2007 and built her wealth through the company's stock. In August 2026 SDI named her its next President & CEO, effective 1 January 2027, succeeding co-founder Mark Millett, who becomes Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: She will become CEO of one of the largest US steelmakers, an electric-arc-furnace producer that has expanded into aluminum (Aluminum Dynamics). That puts her squarely in industrial energy and decarbonisation themes.
deep_cut_fact: She is an avid rock climber who books several climbing trips at the start of each year and tells her team in advance. She nearly took a Chicago consulting job before a mentor steered her to Steel Dynamics to set up its financial reporting.
notes: Strong podcast fit (steel, energy-intensive industry, newly named CEO from Jan 2027). Taylor University accounting graduate; Trine University trustee and 2022 Woman of Distinction honoree. Route through SDI investor relations / corporate office, Fort Wayne (260-969-3500).

name: Archana H Mariwala
current_role: Director, Ascent India Foundation; Marico promoter-group shareholder
profile: Archana Mariwala is the wife of Harsh Mariwala, founder and chairman of Marico (Parachute, Saffola). Her wealth comes from her promoter-group stake in Marico. She has kept a low public profile and has sat on the board of ASCENT, the entrepreneur peer-learning foundation set up by Harsh Mariwala, since 2015.
interesting_fact: ASCENT Foundation, on whose board she sits, is funded by Harsh Mariwala and runs peer-learning groups for growth-stage Indian entrepreneurs. That ties directly to the podcast's entrepreneurship theme.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. Her board role comes from registry data (tofler). Don't confuse her with Archanna Das, ASCENT's CEO. Best route is via the ASCENT Foundation or Harsh Mariwala's office; Harsh is the far more natural podcast guest.

name: Rami Ranger
current_role: Chairman, Sun Mark Ltd and Sea, Air & Land Forwarding Ltd; Conservative life peer (Lord Ranger), House of Lords
profile: Lord (Rami) Ranger, born 1947 in Gujranwala, is a British-Indian entrepreneur. In 1987 he founded freight forwarder Sea, Air & Land Forwarding with £2 and a typewriter, then in 1995 set up Sun Mark, a UK exporter and distributor of FMCG brands. He chairs both companies and has sat in the House of Lords since 2019.
interesting_fact: Sun Mark was the first company to win the Queen's Award for Enterprise in International Trade five years running (2009-2013).
deep_cut_fact: After coming to London in 1971 to study law and running out of money, he worked as a chef at a KFC in Norbury, south London, and rose to district manager. He started SAL Forwarding in 1987 with £2 of capital and a typewriter.

public_contacts.value: contactholmember@parliament.uk (House of Lords member contact; mark for Lord Ranger)

notes: Highly public, media-friendly peer. Some past controversy: Conservative whip withdrawn in 2023 and restored in 2024, CBE revoked in December 2024. Check for sensitivity before outreach. Parliament lists him as member 4729 (not 'Lord Ranger of Northwood'). Sun Mark's site shows only a web-agency email, so use its contact form.

name: D James Bidzos
current_role: Executive Chairman, President & CEO, VeriSign Inc.
profile: Jim Bidzos is a pioneer of commercial internet security. He ran RSA Data Security from 1986 to 1999, co-founded RSA Laboratories, created the RSA Conference in 1991 and founded VeriSign in 1995. He has chaired VeriSign since 2007 and been CEO since 2011. Verisign now runs the authoritative .com and .net registries and two of the internet's 13 root servers.
interesting_fact: He started the RSA Conference in 1991 as a small cryptography gathering; it grew into one of the world's largest cybersecurity events. In the mid-1990s he publicly led the industry campaign against the US government's Clipper chip.
deep_cut_fact: When he joined RSA Data Security on 1 Feb 1986, he later said the company was 'a complete failure'. A toolkit deal with Iris Associates (makers of Lotus Notes) helped turn it around, and by 1993 about 100 companies were using RSA's encryption toolkit.
notes: Rarely gives interviews these days. Strong fit for internet-infrastructure / data-center themes (DNS root operations). Route via Verisign media relations, using the contacts published in the Q3 2026 earnings release.

name: Emanuele Lauro
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Scorpio Tankers (Monaco); Vice Chairman, Cadeler A/S
profile: Emanuele Lauro joined the Monaco-based Scorpio group of shipping companies in 2003 and founded Scorpio Tankers, one of the world's largest product-tanker owners, which he has led as Chairman and CEO since its April 2010 IPO. He also co-founded Eneti (formerly Scorpio Bulkers), which pivoted into offshore-wind installation vessels and merged with Cadeler in December 2023.
interesting_fact: He steered Eneti from dry-bulk shipping into building offshore-wind turbine installation vessels. After its 2023 merger with Cadeler, the world's leading wind-installation vessel operator, he became Cadeler's Vice Chairman, a strong energy-transition angle.
deep_cut_fact: He studied international business at the European Business School, London. He is Vice President of the Monaco Chamber of Shipping and sits on Fordham University's London Advisory Council.
notes: Based in Monaco; brother Filippo Lauro is a Scorpio VP. Very good fit for the energy theme (oil-product shipping plus offshore wind via Cadeler). Route via Scorpio IR.

name: Martha S. Spurlock
current_role: Director, Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. (NASDAQ: CBK) and Commercial Bank (Harrogate, TN); manager, Unified Shares, LLC
profile: Martha Spurlock is a director and roughly 9% beneficial owner of Commercial Bancgroup, the Harrogate, Tennessee parent of Commercial Bank, which listed on Nasdaq in 2025. Her stake is held largely through Unified Shares, LLC, which she has managed since 2014. She has sat on the bank's board since 2016 and the holding company's since 2023.
interesting_fact: Before her bank board career she spent years as a claims service representative at Underwriters Safety & Claims, a workers' compensation insurer, retiring in 2015. She also managed rental properties around Harrogate, Tennessee.

public_contacts.value: ir@cbtn.com (Commercial Bancgroup IR, attn. CFO Philip Metheny)

notes: Private, non-executive shareholder-director of a small Appalachian community bank. No media presence. Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast; reachable only via the company's IR.

name: Phillip A Sharp
current_role: Institute Professor (emeritus), MIT / Koch Institute; Director and SAB chair, Alnylam Pharmaceuticals
profile: Phillip Sharp is a molecular biologist who shared the 1993 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering split genes and RNA splicing. He co-founded Biogen (1978) and Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, the RNAi pioneer, and his wealth comes largely from his Alnylam stake. He remains an MIT Institute Professor and chairs the advisory board of MIT's Jameel Clinic for AI in health.
interesting_fact: He co-founded two of biotech's landmark companies, Biogen and Alnylam. He is the subject of the 2025 documentary 'Cracking the Code: Phil Sharp and the Biotech Revolution'.
deep_cut_fact: Raised on a family farm in a bend of the Licking River near McKinneysburg, Kentucky, he paid his own way to college by raising cattle and growing tobacco. He then attended small Union College in Barbourville, KY.

public_contacts.value: sharppa@mit.edu (MIT faculty email; assistant julialib@mit.edu also listed)

notes: Aged 82; very accessible academic who speaks often on science policy and AI in biology. The MIT faculty email is published on his MIT Biology profile, with an assistant (Julia Libe) listed, so going through the assistant is likely best.

name: Owen Basham
current_role: Partner, Sentinel Capital Partners; Director, Holley Inc. (NYSE: HLLY)
profile: Owen M. Basham (about 40) is a partner at New York private-equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners, which he joined in 2012 after stints at Macquarie Capital's restructuring group and Nancy Creek Capital. He has sat on the board of performance-auto-parts maker Holley since 2018 (public since 2021) and serves on boards of Sentinel portfolio companies such as Empire Auto Parts and RefrigiWear.
interesting_fact: He represents Sentinel, Holley's original private-equity sponsor, on the board. Holley went public in 2021 via a SPAC merger with Empower Ltd. His directors' fees and RSUs are paid to Sentinel, not to him.
deep_cut_fact: Before Holley he helped steer several Sentinel consumer exits, serving on the boards of fast-casual chain Fazoli's, car-wash equipment maker SONNY'S Enterprises and dental group MB2 Dental before their sales. He studied commerce at UVA's McIntire School.
notes: The SEC 'insider holdings' figure likely reflects Sentinel fund-held Holley shares attributed to him as a designee, not personal wealth, so treat the net worth as unreliable. Low public profile; route via Sentinel.

name: Roy Zisapel
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Radware Ltd. (Nasdaq: RDWR)
profile: Roy Zisapel co-founded Israeli cybersecurity and application-delivery company Radware in May 1996 and has been its President & CEO ever since, building it into a global provider of DDoS protection and application security. A Tel Aviv University maths and CS graduate, he also sits on boards across the RAD-Bynet Group, the Israeli tech family of companies.
interesting_fact: He has run Radware as CEO continuously for 30 years, since its founding in 1996, making him one of the longest-serving founder-CEOs on Nasdaq.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Radware in his mid-20s, he worked as a software engineer (1994-96) and an R&D team leader at RND Networks. He is also a director of Bynet Data Centers, a data-center operator in the RAD-Bynet Group, a natural hook for a data-center podcast.
notes: Good fit (cybersecurity, data centers, AI-era app security). He does industry interviews fairly regularly. Route via Radware media relations. Web search budget ran out; facts are from Radware's 2025 20-F and Q3 2026 release.

name: Malynda K West
current_role: President & CEO, Murphy USA Inc. (NYSE: MUSA); Director, Simmons First National Corp.
profile: Mindy West joined Murphy Oil in 1996, working across finance, HR, planning and investor relations. She became CFO of Murphy USA at its 2013 spin-off, took over the fuels business in 2017 and became COO in 2024, President in October 2025 and CEO in January 2026. Murphy USA runs about 1,800+ low-cost fuel and convenience stores (Murphy USA and QuickChek), many next to Walmart.
interesting_fact: She rose from a 1996 finance hire at Murphy Oil to CEO of the spun-off retailer 30 years later. As CFO she also ran its fuel supply and trading organisation from 2017.
deep_cut_fact: She is a director of Ducks Unlimited and its Wetlands America Trust (wetlands conservation), and Vice President of the Razorback Foundation, which supports University of Arkansas athletes.
notes: Goes by 'Mindy' West. Based in El Dorado, Arkansas. Energy and fuel-retail angle. Route via Murphy USA IR; Ash Aulds (ash.aulds@murphyusa.com) is also listed. The store-count figure in the profile was not re-verified this session.

name: Bryan Leach
current_role: Founder, CEO & President, Ibotta, Inc. (NYSE: IBTA), Denver
profile: Born in Nairobi and raised in Atlanta, Bryan Leach studied at Harvard, then Oxford as a Marshall Scholar, then Yale Law. He clerked for Justice David Souter and became a partner at law firm Bartlit Beck before founding cash-back rewards app Ibotta in 2011. Ibotta, which powers digital promotions for retailers such as Walmart, IPO'd on the NYSE in April 2024, the largest tech IPO in Colorado history.
interesting_fact: He came up with Ibotta on a flight while still a law-firm partner, after watching a fellow passenger photograph business cards and receipts to file expenses.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife funded the Leach Center for Performing Arts at Colorado Academy, opened in 2021; the gift also helped start the school's speech and debate program. He also clerked for Justice David Souter at the US Supreme Court.
notes: Media-friendly founder-CEO who talks often about entrepreneurship. Strong fit for the founder-story side of the podcast. Route via Ibotta corporate communications.

name: Douglas K Howell
current_role: Corporate Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. (NYSE: AJG)
profile: Doug Howell, 64, has been CFO of Rolling Meadows, Illinois-based insurance broker Arthur J. Gallagher since 2003. Over that period Gallagher grew through hundreds of tuck-in acquisitions into one of the world's largest insurance brokerage and risk-management firms. His wealth comes from long-held AJG stock and compensation.
interesting_fact: At 23+ years he is one of the longest-tenured CFOs in the S&P 500, serving through Gallagher's transformation into a global broker.
deep_cut_fact: Each quarter Gallagher publishes a separate 'CFO Commentary' alongside its earnings release, a detailed modelling guide for analysts that is closely associated with Howell's investor communication style.

public_contacts.value: sara_walsh@ajg.com (Sara Walsh, company contact on earnings releases)

notes: Low personal media profile; mainly visible on earnings calls. Moderate fit (insurance and risk for energy and data-center assets). Route via Gallagher IR. The 'longest-tenured CFO' ranking is not independently verified; only the tenure since 2003 is sourced.

name: Vance Spencer
profile: Vance Spencer co-founded Framework Ventures with Michael Anderson. It was one of the first VC firms to invest heavily in DeFi and digital assets and has since raised four funds (Funds III and IV were $400M each), expanding into AI, robotics and infrastructure. Framework funds are 10%+ holders of Stablecoin Development Corp (formerly NovaBay) and Better Home & Finance, which explains his SEC insider status.
interesting_fact: Framework's Fund IV (2026, $400M) is pushing beyond crypto into physical AI and robotics. It led Ultra Robotics' $50M Series A and Mecka AI's $60M round, which trains robots on human data.
deep_cut_fact: Before VC, he worked at Netflix (2015-18) in Los Angeles and Tokyo on the relaunch of Netflix Japan. He and Anderson then built and sold Hashletes, an NFL-licensed digital-collectibles startup (2018-19), before founding Framework.
notes: Active on X (@pythianism, linked from his Framework team bio). Good fit for AI and infrastructure themes. His 'net worth' reflects Framework fund holdings attributed to him as a controlling person, not necessarily personal wealth.
